sections.text: As the soul experiences in this body infancy, youth and old age, so finally it passes into another. The wise have no delusion about this.
Those external relations which bring cold and heat, pain and happiness, they come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstance, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, only he is fit for immortality.

We had been discussing Chapter 2, Sankhya Yoga, Yoga of Knowledge. And so far we had seen that just in the beginning, right away, as soon as Bhagavan started his discourse, he came out without waffling about what is the truth. He says, you and I are imperishable.
So are all these people which you see them around you, all these kings. A complete paradigm shift for a normal person who considers himself to be perishable. I was born at one time and Ill die at other time.
In between is my life. So Im a perishable entity. Bhagavan said, no, neither you nor I are perishable.
There was never a time that you did not exist, or I did not exist, or all these people around you did not exist. The existence is permanent. I may not exist in the same form and state.
Im existing today as I existed as a child before and Im existing as an old man now, but still I exist for that I. There is no non existence. So thats a complete paradigm shift and without any explanation.
Bhagavan said, the first thing you should know is youre imperishable. And then he goes into the explanation, because he realized that at the stage Arjuna is in, simple advice like this is your action, these are your duties, you should do this is not enough. Forget about what they did in the past.
Its not going to work. This is a disease which has to be cured at its root cause. The root cause of all the disease or all the problems we have is the desire and attachment which is born out of my ignorance about what the reality is. If Im deluded by this world and my relationship with it, the only way you can cure it is to cure the root cause of it.
Therefore, Bhagavan Buddha said, cure the disease of desire and everything will be cured. No matter how much we help somebody, as long as the root cause is not cured, it will be a band-aid solution as we call it. In architecture, even though the term is borrowed from medicine, we also call it a band-aid solution.
You want to fix it permanently? Well, lets demolish this building and build a new one. Bhagavan realized that just telling Arjuna what is his duty now and what will be right for you is not going to help. Lets start from the beginning.
What is your problem? You are afraid that you will be killing these people? Well, you are incapable of killing these people because they are imperishable. The other day our Dr. Our friend was trying to tell us how indestructible his glasses are.
He said, You know, the one good thing about these glasses.. -- and by the time he finishes the sentence, they broke into two pieces! His whole demonstration of indestructibility fell apart right in front of him. Boy, I need new glasses now. So sometimes what we consider imperishable turns out to be perishable; things we consider indestructible turn out to be quite destructible. So in this life, what I consider is my security blanket, which I consider to be imperishable. Because I think Im in control.
I have taken care of everything. The things which I rely on as dependable may turn out to be undependable. So from Arjunas point of view, he was depending on his teachers and his grandfather -- he thought his family, his dynasty, his culture all depended on them.
And Bhagavan said, that may not be true in the way you think. However, what is true is this: you are indestructible, and they are indestructible at the core of their being. Then he says, why dont I feel it that way? Dehino Asmin Yatha Dehe Kaumaram Yauvanam Jara.
The classical example we use all the time: just as I have changed from my existence as a child to young man to an adult, and I still remain the same. The feeling which I have as I is exactly same today as it was when I was a young man and when I was a child. I always see other people as old people.
I never see myself as old. Its a very strange phenomenon -- I dont know whether anybody can vouch for this. I can tell you, I never feel Im old.
I actually feel the same way as when I was young: I can do that! I look at others and think, these people are old, they cannot do it. Then I realize that person is actually younger than me. You know, Dheerananda used to come to Richmond.
They would say, , let me take your bag. And he would say, Moonkanish, forget it! Im much younger than you are. I have more strength than you do, so dont worry about my bag. But we always feel at the core, core of our heart were indestructible. The same person as I was when I used to have all the real strength.
Thats why the middle aged people go to play the sports which they are supposed not to play at their age. I want to play cricket. I really like cricket because I used to play cricket when I was 20 years old.
Well, you try that today. Then after about two or three games, you realize that thats not the thing you should be doing at the age of whatever you are today. So at the core of your being there is no change.
Change is happening in the outside existence which you have, which is your body. Just as you have changed from a young age to old age. The same way this self will move from one body to another.
He introduces the concept of reincarnation right away. In the first verse he said youre indestructible; in the second verse he says this death is nothing. These are shock treatments to somebody whose mind has gone into a complete delusion.
They cant see the reality as is. And as all these psychiatric treatments used to be shock treatment, you have to jolt him out of that state. Basically, Bhagawan is giving a shock treatment.
We are all deluded by our own reality. Our own security blankets our own thinking about what is right and wrong. And he said, starts from this you are imperishable.
You will continue to exist in one form or another. Therefore, in any culture, and particularly in ours, suicide is never prescribed. Suicide does not solve anything -- it exactly takes the same mental problem you have to the next stage of life.
Youre just running away from your problems. Used to say, if you are unhappy here, if you say, I am so unhappy in us, I am going to go to India and then I will be happy. You will be exactly same unhappy person in India.
Except the place will change. As long as the internal climate you are taking with you, things are not going to change for you. So you have to change your internal climate.
Bhagavan gives you a shock treatment. First: youre imperishable, not perishable. Secondly: death is not going to change anything fundamental -- you will start all over again in a new body.
And then he addresses the question: why then do we feel what we feel in our day to day life? These changes in my life keep occurring -- some are pleasant and some are unpleasant. The answer is in the verse: Matra Sparsaha Tu Kaunteya Sita Ushna Sukha Dukhadaha. Here is the simple analysis of how your experiences are defined.
When your senses come in contact with sense objects, it gives rise to the experience of pleasure and pain, heat and cold. No two people feel the same way about the climate. Somebody in the room, its too hot.
Rajan, can you check another person say Im perfectly fine, dont touch it. Meena will say its too hot and also no, its too cold. And she will say its too cold.
I say no, its too hot. I think our thermostats work differently. Internal thermostats.
So the experience of heat and cold depends on two things. Outside world which has obviously this condition, but also my sensitivity. My senses, its own sensitivity decides whether it is pleasant or unpleasant. s classical example of the cigarette smoker: a cigarette gives one person a heavenly experience.
Im a reform smoker, so I know exactly what Im talking about. When I was in college and when we are in the dining hall, not interested in meal, when can I finish there and go and have a cigarette outside? That was more enjoyable. The cigarette after the dinner or lunch or any time.
Then the lunch itself or dinner itself. Same cigarette gives a repulsive reaction from somebody else. Now Im a reformed smoker, so Im the worst one and I cant really tolerate even the smell of cigarette.
We have one smoker in my office. Every about an hour he goes out, smokes and come back. And then he feels obliged.
Every time he goes out there he needs to say something to me and I say, well, you go away. I really dont want to talk to you right now because youre smelling cigarettes all over my office. The same object which gives pleasure to someone, gives pain to someone.
What it tells you is object has no capacity to give a pleasure or pain. It is your senses which decides which is pleasurable or painful. So Bhagavan said, matras parsaha tu kaunteya sita ushna sukhdukh daha.
This context between the senses and sense objects are the cause of all the experiences you have. So if you remove yourself from the senses because you dont think you are your senses, then these experiences are not yours. Experiences of my car are not Mine.
So my experience of my eyes, I consider mine and I consider my eye to be me. But I dont consider my glasses to be me. My glasses are not me because I can go to lens craft and get it done in one hour.
I know that my eye, I cannot. I have to rely on Santa Ramji and his colleagues to say, make sure that its functioning well because of that attachment, that identification with the eye which makes me feel it is me. But one says this identification with your senses, that your senses are.
You transfer all those experiences to you, whether it is heat or cold, pain or pleasure. So understand, these are not your experiences. These are the experiences of these senses when they come in contact with sense objects.
And it depends on your sensitivity, your sense of you will feel whether pleasure or pain. My mother, I remember she can pick up the burning charcoal and then put it. I said, dont you need it? He said, no, Im fine.
Now I cant even pick up the hot cup of tea because her fingers are numbed by all those cooking. He can pick up charcoal and put it in. When we came to this country, you had to get the fingerprinting done at the airport because you come on a green card.
Well, obviously they have a green card. They make your fingerprint, put it on a green card, sealed it in their plastic and give it. Thats a green card, sir.
Meena comes after me. The guy tried and tried and tried and tried and couldnt get a fingerprint done. Sir, Im sorry, but your wife probably have to go to the downtown in Houston to get this fingerprint done.
We dont have capability to take a fingerprint. I said, whats the problem? He said, because her ridges are all worn out from the chemicals she uses while doing dishes. So we may have special machine in downtown Houston which may be able to do it, but we cant do it.

Krishna offers a profound analogy in verse 13: Just as the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age within this body, so it passes into another body at death. The wise have no delusion about this. We accept the daily changes of our body without confusion about our identity - we do not grieve when our childhood body dies into our adult body. Similarly, the transition from one lifetime to another is simply a continuation of this natural process of change.
Verse 14 introduces the teaching about sensory experiences: Those external relations which bring cold and heat, pain and happiness - they come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely. Notice that the same experience - hot weather, for instance - can be pleasant to one person and painful to another. This proves that the pleasure or pain is not inherent in the object but depends on our own senses and their sensitivity. Understanding this frees us from being enslaved by circumstances.
Today, practice observing your reactions to pleasant and unpleasant experiences with this awareness: This sensation is the result of my senses contacting an object. It is temporary. It will pass. When something uncomfortable happens - physical discomfort, an annoying situation, disappointing news - remind yourself: This too shall pass. And equally, when something pleasant occurs, recognize its temporary nature without clinging. The one who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity is declared fit for immortality. What would it mean to endure bravely the fluctuations of your day?
